headline: Merger costs mask underlying operating strength
summary_short: Revenue jumped 233.8% y/y to $276.8 million as the January 30, 2026 merger with PotlatchDeltic added a new Wood Products segment and two months of consolidated results, but $70.4 million of merger-integration costs swung operating income to a $45.7 million loss and EPS to -$0.05 from $0.17 the prior quarter.
summary_long: The PotlatchDeltic merger-of-equals closed January 30, 2026, adding two months of PCH operations plus a new Wood Products segment ($108.5M sales). Revenue rose 233.8% y/y to $276.8M. Operating income swung to a $45.7M loss on $70.4M of merger costs, partly offset by a $40.3M tax benefit from a valuation-allowance release; net loss was $12.4M (EPS -$0.05). Underlying segments grew: Southern Timber Adjusted EBITDA +68% y/y to $45.5M, Northwest Timber +45% to $8.6M. Real Estate income rose to $27.4M on higher acreage sold. Cash fell to $681.7M; long-term debt rose to $1,855.1M on assumed PCH loans; equity nearly tripled to $5,329.4M on merger stock. Guidance: FY2026 Southern Timber harvest 12.1-12.6M tons, Northwest Timber 2.0-2.3M tons, Wood Products shipments ~1.1B board feet.

drivers.explanation: The PotlatchDeltic merger closed January 30, 2026; results include two new months of consolidated PCH operations and a new Wood Products segment, but $70.4M of merger integration costs drove the reported net loss.
Underlying segments grew despite the reported loss: Southern Timber Adjusted EBITDA +68% y/y to $45.5M and Northwest Timber +45% to $8.6M, both lifted by incremental PotlatchDeltic timberland volume.
Growth driven by consolidating PotlatchDeltic from January 31, 2026, adding the Wood Products segment ($108.5M) and incremental Southern/Northwest Timber harvest volume.
$70.4M of PotlatchDeltic merger integration, employee-related and professional-services costs, booked in Corporate and Other, swung consolidated operating income to a loss.
Merger costs drove the operating loss; a $40.3M tax benefit from releasing a deferred-tax valuation allowance following the merger partly offset it but net income still swung to a loss.
Debt rose on assumption of PotlatchDeltic's term loans in the merger, including 18 acquired interest-rate swaps with $1.037 billion aggregate notional re-designated as cash flow hedges.
Equity nearly tripled on $3.23 billion of total merger consideration, including approximately 140.9 million new Rayonier common shares issued to PotlatchDeltic holders.
Cash fell q/q on $81.1M of dividends paid, $31.1M of share repurchases, $27.5M of mandatory debt repayment and $24.8M of net cash consideration paid in the merger.

MERGER CONTEXT: Rayonier completed a merger-of-equals with PotlatchDeltic Corporation on January 30, 2026 (each PCH share converted to 1.8185 Rayonier shares + $0.61 cash; ~140.9M new shares issued). Consolidated financials include PotlatchDeltic results only from January 31 through March 31, 2026 (two of the quarter's three months), so q/q and y/y deltas on revenue, balance-sheet items and share count reflect both organic growth and the one-time consolidation step-change, not like-for-like comparisons. A new Wood Products segment was added and the former Pacific Northwest Timber segment was renamed Northwest Timber to reflect added Idaho timberlands. Revenue's shard KPI carries Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries provenance ('wire') rather than SEC, but it was cross-checked against the 10-Q's own segment-revenue table ($276.787M) and matches exactly. Short-term debt q/q delta of +0.0% reflects a genuinely flat balance ($199.996M vs $199.982M), not a rounding artifact. EPS and net-income deltas are shown as absolute per-share/dollar changes with a 'swung to loss'/'loss widened' annotation rather than a percentage, since the comparison spans a sign change (profit to loss, or loss widening) where a percentage figure would be meaningless. Guidance entries (Southern/Northwest Timber harvest volumes, Wood Products lumber shipments) were written to the event's guidance[] array from the MD&A Outlook section; no dollar-denominated revenue/EPS guidance was given so guidance_revenue_next_q / guidance_eps_next_q extended metrics were omitted rather than estimated.
